tested_scope: One bounded official-public-documentation leaf. Checked GitHub global node identity semantics and the legacy-to-new global-ID migration path, specifically comparing retained predecessor ID versus lost predecessor ID/current-incarnation-only bootstrap. No repository mutation, paid feature, hosted runner, richer mode, other-role state, downstream/O state, or destructive live predecessor deletion test was used.

observations: REST resources can expose node_id and the same global node ID can be used for GraphQL direct node lookup.
GitHub recommends persisting a global node ID so integrations can continue to reference that object across REST/GraphQL usage.
Global node IDs are to be treated as opaque unique references.

The documented legacy-to-new ID migration starts from a legacy ID already held by the caller and can return the new-format ID for that same object; the documentation does not define a reverse lineage enumeration from an unrelated current repository incarnation to predecessor repository objects.

retained_predecessor_global_id.observation: If the predecessor object's global node ID is already retained and GitHub still resolves that node, direct node lookup can reference that same object. The legacy/new format bridge likewise requires the legacy ID as input.
retained_predecessor_global_id.authority_limit: This is one-way retained-identity continuity, not predecessor discovery from the current incarnation.

lost_predecessor_id_current_id_only.observation: Within the official documentation checked, no provider-supported query is defined that takes only the current repository incarnation's numeric/global identity and returns predecessor owner/name repository incarnations after name reuse/deletion.
lost_predecessor_id_current_id_only.scope_guard: Absence is limited to the documented surfaces checked; it is not a claim about undocumented/internal/future provider metadata.

rename_transfer_then_name_reuse.inference: A unique opaque ID distinguishes the object whose ID was retained, but uniqueness does not itself create a reverse edge from a new current incarnation to a deleted predecessor.

node_or_numeric_id_404.reason: No safe source-qualified deleted predecessor identifier was available in own state, and the bounded lifecycle forbids expanding into a destructive/second probe. Treat unresolved lookup failure as a negative control for the next lineage design, not as observed evidence.

rate_limit_interruption.rule: Any provider lookup interruption must fail closed and checkpoint; it cannot authorize name/incarnation reuse or infer predecessor absence. No same-run wait/backoff/retry is used.

result.new_positive_evidence: Retained GitHub global node IDs are stable opaque object references across REST/GraphQL usage and can bridge legacy/new global-ID formats when the predecessor ID itself is already known.
result.new_falsification: The checked provider identity documentation offers no reverse predecessor-incarnation relation sufficient from current-ID-only bootstrap. Therefore global node identity does not eliminate the lost-predecessor witness problem after logical-name reuse; it only makes a retained predecessor identity useful.
result.minimal_unresolved_child: A zero-cost, non-mutating lineage mechanism that remains reconstructible after provider name reuse when predecessor provider IDs are lost or provider lookups no longer resolve, without external hosted coordination or finite quota.

observation_vs_inference.observed: Documented direct lookup is by an already-held global node ID; documented global-ID migration also begins with an already-held legacy ID.
observation_vs_inference.inferred: Because no checked API relation starts from a distinct current incarnation and enumerates predecessor repository incarnations, current-ID-only recovery needs a separate durable lineage witness or another authority mechanism.

continuation: Part95: execute exactly one bounded repository-local lineage-witness leaf that removes dependence on provider reverse history. Model a single CAS authority record keyed by stable logical resource key with {incarnation_epoch,current_provider_id,predecessor_id_digest_or_tombstone,applied_transition_id}. Required controls: concurrent rename/transfer and name reuse, witness rollback/force-rewind, current-provider-ID change without lineage CAS, ambiguous CAS response, retry/takeover, lost predecessor provider lookup, repository rate-limit interruption, and zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota plus zero incremental cost. Accept only if stale/current-incarnation confusion and duplicate authoritative effects remain fenced under the tested rollback scope; otherwise persist the minimal rollback/anti-ABA residual child and choose a distinct next authority leaf for the following invocation.
